sents.text: Use the least power that works.
Keep Python packages in virtual environments.
And keep your work backed up in Drive and Git, so a mistake is an inconvenience, not a disaster.
In the lab, you'll check who you are, install a small tool with apt, and practise reading commands before you run them.
Prompts and hints, never the full answer.
Root can do anything, and sudo borrows that power for one command.
Use it to change the system, not for pip or your own files.
Read every command before you run it, and check your paths.
Colab runs you as root, so it's your safe practice ground.
